summary:
The SP category is bleeding across the board and it's the clearest signal in the data. All three ratings are cold on sp in the last 14 days — R1 at 41% (76-110), R2 identical at 41% (76-110), and R3 at 45% (83-103) — each flagged 6-8 points below season baseline at a full n=186 sample. That's not noise, that's a category to fade or discount entirely regardless of which rating tier throws it. Meanwhile the strong-play unit ledger confirms the pain is recent, not structural: every rating shows a losing 7-day and 14-day window (R1 -6.0u/-7.0u, R2 -8.0u/-8.0u, R3 -8.0u/-9.0u) even though season-long strong plays remain profitable across the board (R1 +15.0u, R2 +16.0u, R3 +24.0u). R3 is the standout on the longer view — its 30-day strong-play window has already flipped positive (+6.0u, 88-90) while R1 and R2 are still underwater at 30 days (-10.0u and -14.0u respectively), suggesting R3's model calibration is recovering faster from whatever caused this slump.

On category combos, trends + runs remains the top play at 54.6% (213-177, n=390) and trends pairs with anything still clears season baseline — trends+bullpen, trends+hitting, trends+sp all sit in the 52-54% band. Trust trends as the anchor category today. Team-wise, lean into TBR when the model likes them: 70% overall (23-10) and a scorching 78% on strong plays (18-5, +22.0u) — the best combination of volume and unit return on the board. BOS (74%, 26-9) and LAD strong plays (85%, 11-2, +14.0u) are also worth full weight. Fade HOU strong plays hard — 27% (3-8, -8.0u) is the single worst team signal here despite a respectable overall record. Watch the hitting category too: R2 and R3 are both riding 5-game losing streaks there, pairing poorly with the sp cold streak — avoid ratings that lean on sp+hitting combos today.
